messages:
maya singh: heads-up: after yesterday's runtime merge (commit a1b2c3d) canary short-seq p95 jumped ~2.2x. compile queue exploded and kv cache eviction spiked.
tracy chen: yikes. which tests caught it? do we have perf logs? :eyes:
samir patel: quick profiler attached. kernel selector tie-break flipped in a lot of short requests. these are being routed to an int8 kernel that looks good for steady-state but performs worse on short cold KV paths. score diffs tiny (~0.001) but new tiebreaker prefers fresher compiles.
maya singh: tagging infra-bot & deploy-bot for CI and rollout signals.
infra-bot: ci-perf-bench (shortseq) FAILED on 2026-10-09: shortseq_p95 +12% vs baseline.
deploy-bot: canary health check: error_rate +5%, recommend rollback.
oliver k: compile-queue snapshot at peak:
```
$ curl -sS http://internal/compile-queue/api/state | jq '.active|length'
1489
$ curl -sS http://internal/compile-queue/api/recent | jq '. | {queued: .queued[0:5], compiled: .compiled[0:5]}'
{
  "queued": ["job-3312","job-3313","job-3314","job-3315","job-3316"]
}
```
tracy chen: can you paste kernel_selector log for one failing request?
```
kernel_selector: request_id=rc-44
candidates: [fast_fp32, slow_int8]
scores: [0.473, 0.474]
tiebreaker: prefer_newer_compile -> selected slow_int8
reason: score_close && newer_compile_win
```
samir patel: PR #4047 bumped compile_age weight — goal was to avoid stale kernels. but for short sequences, throughput_estimate isn't stable until KV warms, so fresher_compile wins incorrectly.
leo: KV eviction trace shows TTL churn right after the rollout — likely changed selector key ordering in the merge, causing cache key mismatches and rehydration/compiles.
maya singh: proposed immediate actions:
- rollback canary if deploy-bot still recommends
- bisect release to isolate heuristic change (range: HEAD..a1b2c3d)
- hotfix: change tie rule to prefer throughput_estimate when scores are close (|diff| < 0.01)
samir patel: starting automated bisect job now; adding a deterministic shortseq benchmark to ci/bench/shortseq to make this reproducible.
tracy chen: drafting a hotfix patch and will run a canary. patch draft:
```
@@ kernel_selector.py +line 120
- if tie: return prefer_newer_compile(candidates)
+ if tie and abs(score_diff) < 0.01: return prefer_throughput_estimate(candidates)
```
oleg/k: deploying hotfix canary to a shortseq slice at 100 qps.
infra-bot: hotfix deployed to canary-3 at 2111112000, monitoring.
maya singh: also add a regression test to simulate cold KV + short sequences and assert kernel choice stability.
samir patel: bisect narrowed it down: commit a1b2c3d (heuristic config + key-order change). I'll open a revert PR if hotfix doesn't restore baseline. adding a runtime feature flag to gate the new tiebreaker.
tracy chen: canary p95 over 10m window is now +3% vs baseline — much better. extending soak and running a compile-queue stress soak.
leo: drafting issue: "selector key ordering caused KV key churn" with traces attached. recommend follow-ups: revert key-order change, tune compile_age weight, add cache-key unit tests.
maya singh: plan: 1) monitor hotfix canary; 2) if p95 ~ baseline, proceed with gradual rollout + canary expansion; 3) if not, revert merge and follow up with test/weight tuning. :thumbsup:
tracy chen: putting a follow-up note in PR for improved autotune telemetry (emit reasons for tie-break decisions into traces).
samir patel: bisect log and bench results attached to PR #4050. if we revert, include a clear changelog about compile_age behavior and the selector-key-order change.
maya singh: nice triage team. please paste PR links and bench dashboards here when available. will keep this thread open until rollout decision finalized. :rocket:
